record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: If G is a p.o. group which is the intersection of right orders, then can G be order-embedded in an ℓ-group with the embedding preserving any existing sups and infs?

evidence.quote: 1.42. If G is a p.o. group which is the intersection of right orders, then can G be order-embedded in an ℓ-group with the embedding preserving any existing sups and infs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a partially ordered group (a group equipped with a translation-invariant partial order ≤, i.e., a ≤ b implies xay ≤ xby for all x,y ∈ G). A right order on G is a total order ≼ on G that is right-invariant (a ≼ b implies ax ≼ bx for all x). Assume that the partial order on G is the intersection of a family of right orders on G; that is, for a, b ∈ G, a ≤ b in G if and only if a ≼ b for every right order ≼ in this family.

A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group L with a translation-invariant partial order under which (L, ≤) is a lattice (every pair of elements has a supremum and an infimum). An order-embedding of G into L is an injective group homomorphism φ : G → L such that for all a, b ∈ G, a ≤ b in G if and only if φ(a) ≤ φ(b) in L. Such an embedding is said to preserve existing sups and infs if whenever sup S exists in G for a subset S ⊆ G, then sup φ(S) = φ(sup S) in L, and analogously for infima.

Question: Can every such partially ordered group G (that is realized as an intersection of right orders) be order-embedded into an ℓ-group via an embedding that preserves all existing suprema and infima in G?
